answer: A provider convicted of Medicaid fraud faces mandatory exclusion from all federal health care programs for a minimum of 5 years.

citations.quote: Mandatory exclusions are effective for a minimum of 5 years, but aggravating factors may lead to a longer or permanent exclusion.

Providers and suppliers face mandatory exclusions if they’re convicted of these offenses: ● Medicare or Medicaid fraud, as well as any other offenses related to delivering items or services under Medicare or Medicaid
The Exclusion Statute requires OIG to exclude health care providers and suppliers from participating in all federal health care programs if they’re convicted of certain offenses.

gold_answer: A mandatory exclusion lasts a minimum of 5 years. Aggravating factors can make it longer or permanent.
gold_quote: Mandatory exclusions are effective for a minimum of 5 years, but aggravating factors may lead to a longer or permanent exclusion.

judge.rationale: The answer correctly gives the 5-year minimum mandatory exclusion, which directly answers the question even without the aggravating-factor detail, and P1 and P2 support every claim.
